data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Aqif means 'the one who keeps awake'. This name is derived from the Quranic verse, 'And keep up prayer and give zakat and hold in honour the bond of Allah.' This 'Aqif is also known for his debates with the Muħtazila scholars, particularly al-Jahiz and al-Nafs al-Zaki. He was a strong defender of orthodox Sunni theology and opposed the Muħtazila doctrines, which were seen as deviating from the traditional Islamic beliefs.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hadid (d. 1252 CE) The name Aqif carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In his work 'Sharh Nahj al-Balagha' (Commentary on the Sayings of the Prophet), Ibn Abd al-Hadid mentioned a scholar named 'Aqif ibn Makram, who was a companion of Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 795 CE) and one of the earliest scholars of the Maliki school of law.
